lines:
Removed the duplicated shell/Python execution modes and made the effective tool set resolve interface-from-build, authority-from-Chat.

Landed:
1. tool_loop.rs - deleted both `if jobs::controls_available(&self.context.bindings)` forks; shell and python now have exactly one implementation each (start_shell_job / start_python_job, 10s soft wait). Deleted host_process_result_value and host_process_result_summary, the only emitter of "was killed after the {n} second limit expired"; zero references remain. timeout_seconds is destructured as `_` and is no longer a deadline; removed the unused ProcessTermination and ControlledProcessResult imports. Added pub(crate) implied_job_control_ids: a bound host shell/Python capability implies job.output, job.input, job.stop, job.list, job.keep.
2. pipeline/frozen_tools.rs - single entry `effective(requested, previous)`: requested capabilities plus implied controls, frozen from this build, then authority restored from the saved Chat (options/executable, requires_approval, secret, file_access_version, internal_id). `complete_saved` re-resolves a stored Chat's interface from this build, reconstructing credential bindings from the stored secret so web-search key requirements still validate.
3. pipeline.rs - freeze path uses `effective`; the agent node tool set gains the implied controls so the model is offered them.
4. pipeline/continuation.rs - an existing Chat re-resolves its bindings (complete_saved), extends the worker allowlist (agent_checkpoint.config.allowed_tool_capability_refs, enforced in aworkit-workflow-worker/src/agent.rs:319) and the manifest (broker authority boundary) for capabilities it did not have before. Restructured into two disjoint steps to avoid holding the budget borrow across a &mut saved.
5. Docs and text: docs/shell-jobs.md rewritten to one contract (no second mode, no "start a new Chat"); the bundled tool plugin no longer describes a legacy mode or "requires ... in this Chat"; the native smoke script's 'legacy' phase replaced by an 'implied' phase asserting that a Chat whose workflow never selected the control tools still yields a jobId and can stop it.

Verification: `cargo check --lib --tests` finishes with no errors and no warnings after every step. The bundled tool plugin still parses as valid JSON (json.loads). No unit-test fixture binds tool.shell.host/tool.python.host, so the implied-control change does not alter existing fixture binding counts (reasoned from the fixtures, not executed).

NOT verified, with causes:
- `cargo test` cannot build in this environment: the test profile must compile C dependencies (ring, aws-lc-sys, tree-sitter, libsqlite3-sys, vswhom-sys) and `cl.exe` is not on this shell's PATH (ToolNotFound). Needs an MSVC environment (vcvars / Developer Command Prompt). No test was executed; runtime behaviour is unproven.
- desktop/scripts/native-shell-jobs-smoke.mjs was not run for the same reason (it needs a built app).
- The running desktop app is the previous build, so the change is not observable until the app is rebuilt.

Remaining after this task: (a) later passes still take node/tool definitions from the saved snapshot, so adding a brand-new tool to the workflow and continuing in the same Chat needs the current-document resolution required by the design (follow-up task created); (b) the four job-control tools are still user-facing Settings switches although they no longer gate behaviour, so the Settings surface still shows redundant toggles; (c) shell_start/python_start remain separate immediate-return entry points that now share one code path with shell/python and could be folded into them.

Replace the duplicated shell/Python execution modes with one managed job path, and stop pinning tool interfaces to a Chat.

Reproduction (2026-09-19, this Chat, python tool, no job controls bound): script printing "start" then sleeping 40s returned exitCode 1, termination "timed_out", partial stdout "start", no jobId. Confirms the legacy blocking branch is live and that a Chat cannot obtain managed jobs without the four control tools frozen.

Atomic edit set (all three parts must land together; removing the legacy branch alone would leave a Chat unable to collect job output):

1. Single execution mode - desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/tool_loop.rs
   - FileToolDispatcherV1::execute ~2622-2664 (Shell) and ~2666-2709 (Python): delete the `if jobs::controls_available(...)` fork and the whole legacy branch; always call start_shell_job / start_python_job.
   - Delete now-dead host_process_result_value (~3308) and host_process_result_summary (~3329), the only emitter of "was killed after the {n} second limit expired". Verify no other callers.
   - Drop imports that become unused (ProcessTermination; BuiltInProcessTools/NativeProcessPort/HostToolLimitsV1 remain used by jobs.rs).

2. Job control is intrinsic - tool_loop/jobs/contract.rs + jobs.rs
   - controls_available becomes an invariant (job tools accompany host shell/Python), not a per-Chat gate chosen by four unrelated switches.
   - start_process_job guard in jobs.rs:125 becomes an assertion with a precise message.
   - completed_tool_bindings(): when the frozen set binds tool.shell.host or tool.python.host, add the job control bindings (jobs::IDS) with their model definitions, so the model can see and call them.

3. Interface resolved at dispatch, authority frozen - tool_loop.rs + pipeline.rs
   - Refresh provider_name/description/input_schema/limit of built-in bindings from the current build via freeze_file_tool_bindings, keeping capability_id, requires_approval, secret, file_access_version, internal_id from the saved binding.
   - Apply the completed+refreshed set before compile_graph_snapshot / compile_graph_pass, before FrozenFileToolAuthorityContextV1.bindings (pipeline.rs ~934 and ~2285), and append the missing capability bindings to the manifest so prepare_broker accepts a job call (tool_loop.rs ~1968).
   - Continuation path: pipeline.rs:561 continuation::prepare plus the saved record reuse must use the same effective set.

4. Docs and tests
   - docs/shell-jobs.md: one contract; remove the legacy-mode and "start a new Chat" passage; job control is not separately switchable.
   - Update tests that pin the legacy behaviour or the four-tool gate; keep the settings health probes (settings_diagnostics.rs) which legitimately use a bounded deadline.

Verification status: incremental `cargo check --lib` in desktop/src-tauri works (0.57s when clean), so edits are checkable; a full post-edit crate rebuild may exceed the 30s legacy kill in a Chat without job controls, so verification may need a Chat with job controls or a foreground build outside the agent.

Acceptance: one behaviour for shell/python in every Chat; no reachable path emits the 30-second kill message; existing and new Chats both obtain and can collect managed jobs.

data.title: Remove the duplicated shell/Python execution modes and resolve tool interfaces at dispatch
